Hubibur Rahman Khan with Farmanullah Khan and S.A. Latif ------ For the Petitioner.
Amirul Kabir Choudhury ------ For the O.P.
parties:
Musa Bin Shamser ------ Petitioner.
Vs.
Ansarul Huq Ansari & others ------ Opp. Parties.
full_judgment:
Fazle Hussain Mohammed Habibur Rahman J.-- This Rule at the instance of accused Musa Bin Shamsher under section 561A Cr.P.C. was issued calling upon the Deputy Commissioner, Chittagong and the complainant opposite party No. 1 Ansarul Huq Ansari to show cause why the proceedings in G.R. Case No. 50/85 pending in the Court of the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Chittagong should not be quashed. 

 2. The facts of the case are as follows:- On 12.1.85 complainant Ansarul Huq Ansari of P.S. Panchlaish, District Chittagong lodged a complaint in the Court of the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Chittagong alleging that accused petitioner Musa Bin Shamsher, Proprietor, MIS. Delco International, 47 B, Road No.11 Banani P.S. Gulshan, Dhaka and 41/1, Dilu Road, P.S. Ramna, Dhaka became known to the complainant in Qatar City in course of business. The complainant used to carry-on business in Qatar by residing there for a long time. The accused used to come to the house and office of the complainant in Qatar often. Accused petitioner showed him a power of attorney issued by the Government of Qatar in favour of his firm M/s. Shahbaz International, Topkhana Road, Dhaka and proposed to do joint business in N.O.C.-Visa with him. Complainant in good faith believed the statement of the accused and said that returning to Bangladesh in consultation with his relations he would take a decision to do the business of N.O.C. visa. Accused subsequently said in Qatar that he had arranged for one N.O.C. permit and to complete formalities of the permit he wanted to have a loan of some money from the complainant but the complainant expressed his inability. The cunning accused on 30.8.79 011 promise to arrange within three months N.O.C. (Visa) for 20/22 poor relations of the complainant at the rate of Tk  40000/- each took Tk. 8,00,000/- from the complainant in equivalent Qatar currency. Accused came to Bangladesh and wrote letters to the complainant at Qatar explaining various reasons and official difficulties regarding delay in supplying N.O.C. Visas. The complainant in good faith believed the statements of the accused. The complainant returned to Bangladesh in 1980 and met the accused who said that in order to meet the official anomalies it would not be possible to procure the N.O.C., Visa and (work) permits unless more money was paid, otherwise the money which has already been spent would be lost. Accused proposed that he would execute an agreement in favour of the complainant to supply him 20/22 N.O.C.-Visa if the complainant paid the accused Tk.12,00,000/- more for the purpose of making payments to different organizations to meet the official anomalies. On 2.6 80 the complainant in good faith in presence of witnesses paid Tk. 12,00,000/- more to the accused at complainant's house at 981, O R. Nizam Road, Chittagong. The accused on that date (2.6.80) acknowledged the receipt of a total amount of Tk. 20,00,000/- at complainant's said house by executing a Chuktipatra" (agreement) on a non-judicial stamp paper worth Tk. 3/-. In terms of the agreement the accused undertook to perform the entire responsibility of the proposed joint business of obtaining 20/22 N.O.C.-Visa, work permit, etc. for the relations of the complainant and hand them over to him. 

 4. The complaint also filed the "Chuktipatra" (agreement) dated 2-6-80 in which it is stated by the accused that when demanded by the complainant he would be bound to refund the said amount of Taka twenty lacs within 6 months from the date of demand and that if he cheated the complainant of the money paid to him or criminally misappropriated the said amount in any manner he would be liable to be prosecuted in the criminal court and that action in the Civil Court also would lie. In the petition of complaint M.M. Akbar, Shahid Zafar, Abdul Baten, etc. were named as witnesses. The learned Magistrate examined the complainant on 12-1-85 on solemn affirmation and the complainant stated as follows: 

 5. The Chief Metropolitan Magistrate after examining the complainant issued warrant of arrest against the accused U/Ss 406 and 420 of the Penal Code on 12-1-85. On 5-3-85 the accused surrendered before the court and prayed for bail. The accused was released on bail on that date. As accused I remained absconding, the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate asked the sureties to produce him in court within 21-4-85. But on 18-4-85 the Sessions Judge, Chittagong stayed further proceedings and called for the record in Criminal Motion No. 261/85. 

 6. In the petition before this Court the case for the defence has not been stated. It appears that while filing a petition for ball in the trial court it was stated on behalf of the accused that the accused has been falsely implicated in this fabricated case out of enmity and grudge started on the basis of a forged document created for the purpose of this case to harass the accused. It is pointed out on behalf of the complainant opposite party that apparently with a view to deny his signature in the Chuktipatra (agreement) the accused has started signing his name in the vokalatnama, etc. in a different manner. 

 7. The learned Additional Sessions Judge, 1st Court Chittagong heard the motion u/s.439A Cr.P.C. for setting aside the order dated 12-1-85 taking cognizance of the offence and issuing warrant against accused u/s 406 and 420 of the Penal Code. The learned Additional Sessions Judge, 1st Court Chittagong rejected the motion under section 439A Cr. P. C. on 12-11-85 with the following observation. 

 "On perusal of the record it appears that petition of complainant was filed u/ss. 406/420/500 of the Penal Code and the learned Magistrate after examining the complainant on S/ A issued warrant of arrest against the accused for the offences u/s. 406 and 420 of the Penal Code. Whether any of the sections mentioned in the petition of complaint has been prima facie made out can best be decided by the trial court. ..... ". 

 Thereafter the accused petitioner obtained this Rule from this court on 24-11-85. 

 8. Mr. Habbibur Rahman Khan, the learned Advocate for the accused petitioner submits that from the petition of complaint it appears that the complainant opposite party has invested Tk. 20,00,000/- for joint business of N.O.C. (manpower) with the accused petitioner on the basis of an agreement executed 011 2-6-80 by the accused petitioner. He submits that the alleged payments having been made in a joint business (Joutha Karbar) or a business of partnership neither there can be a case of entrustment nor there can be a case of deception against the accused. The learned Advocate for the petitioner refers to the decisions in the cases of Nasiruddin Mahmud and others rs. Momtazuddin Ahmed and another, 36 DLR (4D) 14, Bhuban Mohan Das, Vs. Surendra Mohan Das AIR 1951 Calcutta (FB) 69 and Velji Raghavji Paten VS The State of Maharashtra, AIR 1965 (Se) 1433. He further submits that the use of the work "Joutha Karbar" (joint business) in the 'Chuktipatra' as well as in the petition of complaint means the business of partnership, that there can not be any criminal breach of trust against one partner by another" partner because the very concept of partnership precludes the possibility of entrustment or dominion of the partnership pro party by one partner against the other. He also submits that there is no special fiduciary relationship between the parties, that a partner cannot proceed against another partner of a partnership business for an alleged offence of criminal breach of trust in respect of partnership property and that the share of a partner in the assets of the firm cannot be determined until an account has been taken and all the debts have been discharged and as such the only remedy of the complainant opposite party as co-partner in the facts of the partnership itself is in the competent civil court. He further submits that the dispute is purely of a civil nature, that the accused has committed no criminal offence of cheating and dishonest misappropriation and therefore the criminal proceedings should be quashed against the accused petitioner. 

 In Mollwo  March & Co vs. The Court of Wards (1872) LR. 4. PC. 419 it was observed that whether relation of partnership in business does or does not exist must depend on the real intention and contract of the parties. In the present case when we confronted the learned advocate for the petitioner with the question whether the accused petitioner admits that he has taken Taka twenty lacs from the complainant for supplying to him 20/22 NOCs Visas. work permits for his relations on the plea of joint business and executed the agreement on 2.680 in presence of witnesses and whether the accused is prepared to admit such fact in writing under his signature or by swearing an affidavit to that effect, the learned advocate submits that in a criminal case the accused has no obligation to disclose his version of the case. He, however, concedes that since the complainant says in his complaint that the accused falsely denied the entire transaction of accepting Taka twenty lacs from the complainant undertaking to supply 20/22 N.O.Cs., visas, permits etc. to the complainant, we have to accept that statement as prima facie correct at this stage. Therefore, in the facts of the present case when according to the complainant the accused denied the entire transaction cheated the complainant and dishonestly misappropriated the money, there is no basis for this court to hold that there was a partnership between the complainant and the accused. 

 13. The decisions in the cases of M. Mahmud, vs. M Ahmed, 36 DLR (AD) 14 and Velji Raghavji Patel vs. The State of Maharashtra, AIR 1965 (SC) 1433 have referred to several decisions to consider the question whether charge u/s. 406 of the Penal Code can stand in respect of property belonging to the partners. The Appellate Division of the Supreme Court of Bangladesh as well as the Supreme Court of India approved the view taken by Harries, C. J. expressed in the decision of the Full Bench of five judges of the Calcutta High Court in the case of Bhuban Mohan Das vs. Surendra Mohan Das, AIR 1951 Calcutta (FB) 69. Relying on the decision in the case of Piddocke vs. Butt, (1894) I Ch, 343 it was held by the Full Bench of Calcutta High Court consisting of 5 Judges in the said case of Bhuban Mohan Das, AIR. 1951 Calcutta (FB) 69 as follows: 

 14. In the said case of Bhuban Mohan Das vs. Surendra Mohan Das, AIR 1951 Calcutta (F B)  69 the Full Bench also considered the Full Bench decision of five Judges of the Bombay High Court in the case of Lall Chand Roy, 9 WR (Cr) 37. In the said case of Lall Chand Roy the question referred was, "whether if a partner dishonestly misappropriates or converts to his own use or dishonestly uses or disposes of any of the partnership property which he is entrusted with. or has dominion over, he is guilty of an offence punishable under the Penal Code. "The question submitted to the Full Bench of the Bombay High Court was answered in affirmative. Harries, C.J. delivering the judgment of the Full Bench of the Calcutta High Court in the case of Bhuban Motion Das, A I.R. 1951 Calcutta (F,B) 69 considered this case and partly agreed with one part of the decision and observed that the said Full Bench decision of the Bombay High Court is certainly authority for the proposition that if by special arrangement between the parties One partner could be regarded as being entrusted with property, in such circumstances a partner can be charged u/s. 406 of the Penal Code. Harries, C.J. observed as follows, 

 "Ofcourse if it could be made out that one partner had been entrusted with property or with dominion over it, no difficulty would arise ................................... It may be that by special arrangement between the parties one partner could be regarded as being entrusted with property................................. This Full Bench case (of Bombay High Court) is certainly authority for the proposition that in some circumstances a partner can be Charged u/s, 406, Penal Code. But it is not very helpful, with great respect, to a court which is called upon to decide whether a partner receiving a partnership asset in his capacity as a partner is guilty of fraudulent breach of trust if he did not account for it............................................A person who receives property in a fiduciary capacity must deal with the property according to the terms of the arrangement or trust. He cannot dispose of the property as he likes and claim to account for it at some later stage. ....................... 

 16. In the case of N. Mahmud Vs. M. Ahmed 36 DLR (AD) 14 the facts were that the complainant and the accused persons came from the same locality of Noakhali, that the accused persons had taken at Khulna from the complainant a sum of Tk. 25,500/- for the purpose of their business between 18-1-74 to 1-5-74, that accused No. 1 issued two cheques totaling  Tk 25,500/- towards repayment but informed by telegram that these cheques need not be presented as there was shortage of money in his account, that subsequently the parties made up their affair, that on the proposal of the complainant the accused persons agreed to work for him in his new venture in M/S Linker Enterprise, that the complainant allowed thrill tile facility to work in the said new venture for the purpose of realizing his money, that" according to the defence it was the result of the partnership arrangement and deed  was executed on 26-4-76" (it is not manifest from the cited decision as to how the admission of the accused regarding the alleged partnership arrangement on the basis of execution of a deed on 26-4-76 was introduced by the accused in a partition for quashing under section 561A Cr.P .C), that accused petitioner received a sum of Tk. 44,661/- on different dates for the purpose of the business that instead of depositing this amount in the account of Linker Enterprise in Uttara Bank, Khulna the accused No. 1 opened another account in the name of Linker Enterprise showing him as the owner of the firm with the Sonali Hank, Khulna being account No. C. A. No. 5592 and deposited the various amounts received on behalf of the Linker Enterprise, that the accused misappropriated the said amount, that accused Nos.1 and 3 withdrew Tk. 14,756/- from the business fund on the plea of marriage ceremony of the sister of accused No.1 and that accused Giasuddin and accused No 1 took away Tk. 5000/- from the business of the complainant and [bat those amounts were taken without the consent of the complainant, So it appears that in the case of Nasiruddin Mahmud, 36 DIR (AD) 14 the accused positively admitted the deed executed on 26-4-76 and the accused did not deny any of the transactions (although, as already stated, it is not evident from the cited decision as to how the admission of accused regarding the alleged partnership arrangement on the basis of execution of a deed dated 26-4-76 was introduced by the accused in petition under section 561 A Cr.P.C. for quashing). 

 17. In these circumstances the Appellate Division in Nasiruddin Mahmud’s Case, 36 DLR (AD) 14 held that there was a partnership business, that all the transactions were in course of the partnership business and that, therefore, in view of the decision  in the case of Bhuban Mohan Das AIR 1951Calcutta (FB) 69 as referred to with approval of the Supreme Court of India in the case of Velji Baghavji Patel, AIR 1965 (SC) 1433 prosecution for criminal misappropriation u/s 406 of the Penal Code, cannot be maintained. Regarding the question of commission of offences of cheating punishable u/s. 420 of the Penal Code the Appellate Division observed in the said case of N. Mahmud Vs. N. Ahmed, 36 DLR (AD) 14 as follows:
